newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: BORBIDGE SAYS HE'S HAPPY WITH CENTURY ZINC PROGRESS
Queensland Premier, Rob Borbidge, says he's pleased with the reponse of Aborigines to the appointment of Bill Hayden as the Government's negotiator for the Century Zinc mine.
In Burketown yesterday, Mr Borbidge said talks between Gulf Aborigines and Mr Hayden are progressing well.
Mr Borbidge said he also had a brief and cordial meeting with Aboriginal Activist, Murrandoo Yanner.
COLLINGWOOD LOSES GREAT
Collingwood Football club has lost one of its favourite sons, with the passing yesterday of former champion player, Bill Twomey.
One of four brothers, three of whom played for the Magpies, Bill Twomey was known as a brilliant but sometimes erratic player, who appeared in 189 senior matches for Collingwood.
Club president, Kevin Rose, says he was a great part of
Collingwood.
A Funeral will be held for Bill Twomey tomorrow morning at Balwyn.
AID GIVES AUSTRALIA MORE INFLUENCE IN VIETNAM
The Parliamentary secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Andrew Thomson, says aid money is enhancing Australia's political influence in Vietnam.
Mr Thomson is in Vietnam to familiarise himself with the aid programme.
He's also used the visit to lobby Hanoi over a failed 300-million dollars investment project, and says it's an example of Australia's aid programme giving him access to more senior levels of
government.
COSTELLO SAYS IR POLICY DINKI-DI
Federal Treasurer Peter Costello says the Government's wages and industrial relations policy will be a dinki-di Australian model, and not a copy of any other country's policies.
Mr Costello is in Washington for the annual meeting of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
He says he won't try to emulate the Americans with low wages and low unemployment, or the Europeans with high wages and high unemployment.
The Treasurer says the Government's policy will be a great
improvement to how idustrial relations is conducted in Australia.
MAHATIR WARNS OF FUNNY REMARKS
Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohammed says Australia and Malaysia are on friendly terms, although any "funny remarks" about Malaysia could harm the relationship.
Doctor Mahathir, who in the past has used strains in the relationship with Australia to gain political mileage at home, was speaking to journalists in Kuala Lumpur.
Bilateral relations hot an all-time low in 1993 when former Prime Minister Paul Keating decribed the Malaysian leader as
recalcitrant.
AFL TRADING DAY OVER
To Football, and the AFL's trading day has ended with Anthony Rocca, Todd Viney and Leigh Colbert, attracting the attention of new clubs.
While Geelong is believed to be keen to re-sign Colbert, Rocca appears determined to leave Sydney for a Melbourne-based club, but has put a high price on his head.
Former South Australian, Viney is being touted as a possible recruit for Port Power.
In other news, there's widespread speculation, South Australian Commissioner, Wayne Jackson will today be named the AFL's new Chief Executive.
NATIONAL STANDARDS FOR TEACHERS
The Federal Government's about to start work on the first set of national standards for the education of teachers.
Education Minister, David Kemp, says the new standards will be finalised by April next year.
He says its vital that teachers are educated to meet the changing needs of students and schools.
QLD BALLET TO TOUR US

The Queensland Ballet Company has been recognized on the international stage with dancers about to leave for the United States on their first major overseas tour The seven week tour opens in Los Angeles in a week's time and finishes in New York at the end of November.
Queensland Ballet Artistic Director, Harold Collins, says the tour
is a milestone for the company.
Mr Collins says the tour will be tremendous professional development for the dancers with American teachers working with the company.
NEW METHOD TO MAKE ONE-DAY CRICKET FAIRER
A new method to make rain interrupted one-day cricket matches
fairer has received in-principle approval from the International Cricket Board.
Professor Tony Lewis of the UK has explained his method to the Mathematics and Computers in Sport conference on the Gold Coast.
Professor Lewis says his method is fairer, because it takes account of the stage of the innings when the overs are lost, and also the wickets that have been lost.
He's outlined his proposal to the International Cricket Board, and expects it to be trialled in the international arena next year.
SURFING VYING FOR OLYMPIC INVOLVEMENT
As the World Surfing Games get underway this weekend at
California's Huntington Beach, a major push is underway to have surfing including as a medal sport at the Sydney Olympics.
International Olympic Committee delegates will be present during the competition which will field around 600 surfers from 40 nations.
Aussie team coach "Rabbit" Bartholomew says surfing's competing with other fringe sports for a spot in the 2000 games.
He says the sport has had some kind of a commitment it'll be involved, probably as a cultural sport.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
